label: The last pass over an exported film: open and close on a fade, and captions burnt in

params.name: fade_in_seconds
params.label: Open from black over this many seconds (0 = cut straight in)

params.name: fade_out_seconds
params.label: Close to black over this many seconds (0 = cut straight out)

params.name: fade_sound
params.label: Bring the sound up and down with the picture

params.name: caption_font_size
params.label: Caption size, in points of a 384-point-tall frame (libass scales it to the real frame)

params.name: caption_colour
params.label: Caption colour, in the subtitle format &HAABBGGRR (00 = solid)

params.name: caption_outline_colour
params.label: Outline colour, same format - an outline is what keeps words readable over any picture

params.name: caption_border_style
params.label: 1 = outline round the letters, 3 = a solid box behind them

params.name: caption_margin
params.label: How far the captions sit from the bottom edge

params.name: caption_alignment
params.label: Where the captions sit: 2 = bottom centre, 8 = top centre (subtitle numbering)

params.name: caption_main_font
params.label: The captions' main font (tv/fonts): Latin letters, digits and signs. A script it lacks (Hindi, Telugu...) comes from that script's own Noto font, the same size family

description_nl: 2026-09-20, the editing pass: a film that cuts in hard from nothing and stops dead reads like a clip, not a film, so the export opens and closes on a short fade - picture and sound together - without changing its length by a frame. Captions are the subtitle file the Sound step already writes (film.srt), burnt into the picture for the places that play a video silently; the words are never retyped, so they always match what was spoken. Whether captions go on is asked per export (the person ticks the box); everything about how they LOOK is here. Set both fades to 0 and the picture is passed through as it was.
weight_basis: How the last pass looks. The person ticks captions on or off per export; the numbers live here.
